Asha P: quick accessibility review from today's console QA pass — two small but important nits around the Filters panel and the Apply modal. Noah (Eng): ok what did you find? Asha P: 1) When filters update, the visual badge count changes but there's no SR announcement. Screen reader users don't get feedback that results changed. 2) The Apply modal traps focus but doesn't expose role=dialog with aria-modal=true consistently; also the close button is hard to hit via keyboard in compact layouts. Derek (PM): for the filter counts, do we want an aria-live region or change the button label dynamically? What's the less noisy pattern? Iris - QA: aria-live polite region that announces "Filters applied, 12 results" is usually fine and less disruptive. We should debounce updates so it doesn't repeat while someone is toggling a multi-select. Noah (Eng): implementation idea: a visually-hidden
that we update after the debounce on filter apply. Where should it live in DOM? top of the list? Asha P: put it near the list heading so SR users get context. Use aria-atomic to ensure full phrase read. Example text: `Filters applied. Showing 12 models. Filter: tag:research, stage:beta.` Keep it concise. Noah (Eng): got it. we'll also need to avoid announcing when the counts change due to pagination or sorting — only announce when filters themselves change. Derek (PM): good point. Add a small flag to the state: announceOnFilterChange. Iris - QA: 2) About the Apply modal: VoiceOver on Mac reads "dialog" but NVDA doesn't announce because role attribute missing on nested markup. We switch between two modal implementations in different pages. Need consistent dialog markup: role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby=headingId and focus trap. Noah (Eng): current modal lib sets role but our wrapper sometimes gets removed by CSS-only hiding. I'll standardize to a single modal component and ensure the outer element has role=dialog. Asha P: keyboard nit: when the modal opens, focus lands on the first tabbable element (first input). Good. But when closing, focus should return to the Filter button that opened it. Right now it lands on body. Remember to persist opener in a data attribute and restore focus on close. Noah (Eng): will do. Also saw that the close 'X' button has only a 16x16 clickable area visually. For keyboard and touch it's fine but let's make hit target >= 24px and ensure focus-visible ring is prominent. Derek (PM): tie-back to design tokens: what's the recommended focus halo color for the light theme? We have a high-contrast token but it looks too blue against white in tests. Asha P: for light theme use #0a84ff with 2px solid + 4px semi-transparent halo; ensure contrast >= 3:1 for the stroke against the background behind it. For dark theme use the teal token we discussed earlier. Iris - QA: I'll capture screenshots for styling and add Playwright checks: one for aria-live text present after filter apply, one for modal role and focus return. Noah (Eng): code snippet for announcer update: ```js // after debounce when filters change const announcer = document.getElementById('filter-announcer'); announcer.textContent = `Filters applied. Showing ${count} ${count > 1 ? 'models' : 'model'}.`; ``` And modal focus restore: store opener: `const opener = document.activeElement; openModal(); // on close: opener?.focus();` Asha P: small SR wording suggestion: avoid punctuation that causes odd pauses. Use natural phrasing: "Filters applied. Showing twelve models." Consider spelling out numbers under 10? No need unless tests require it. Derek (PM): timeline? sounds like low-effort. Noah, can you scope PR? Noah (Eng): yes — announcer + focus restore + hit target tweak in a single small PR. I'll also normalize modal instantiation. D: 2 days. Iris - QA: i'll add tests (D: 2 days) and run NVDA/VoiceOver passes after PR. A11yBot: automated scan summary: 2 issues reported earlier: missing live announcer, inconsistent dialog role. Saved failing traces to /tests/fixtures/filter-modal-a11y.json Asha P: follow-ups: - Noah: PR for announcer + modal consistency + close target (D: 2 days) - Iris: playbook tests + SR pass (D: 2 days) - Derek: update ticket priority to P2, escalate if customer report arrives. Noah (Eng): will include sample unit test for the announcer and a short note in the component docs. Derek (PM): thanks team! :raised_hands: Iris - QA: ping me when ready, i'll run with VoiceOver on CI. :white_check_mark:
